page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-16xCPU-64GB is a general-purpose virtual machine within the Cloud Native family, running on the KVM hypervisor. It is provisioned with 16 shared vCPUs mapped to AMD EPYC 7542 processors operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware cache includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity is set to 64.0 GB RAM, providing a balanced 1:4 allocation of 4.0 GB of memory per core. The instance provides no integrated local storage and contains zero GPUs.

Benchmark measurements indicate consistent mid-tier compute and memory bandwidth capabilities across general-purpose metrics. Multi-threaded processing reaches a Geekbench multi-core score of 15,148.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 25,240.42, accompanied by 11,615.41 on stress-ng multi-core testing. In contrast, stress-ng single-core compute performance registers at 785.98 in the bottom 10%, though Geekbench single-core reaches 2,056.0. Memory bandwidth delivers 47.62 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads but drops to a weaker 19.49 GB/sec for large-block writes. In-memory caching registers 17.27 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks.

Tradeoffs center around the shared CPU allocation, the lack of local disk volumes, and subdued generation rates for larger compute tasks. LLM text generation on a 7B parameter model yields 4.92 tokens per second, falling into the bottom 10%. Furthermore, static web serving throughput measures at 4.96 GB/sec. Because storage is not bundled, operators must attach network storage volumes separately. These properties make UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-16xCPU-64GB an efficient allocation for microservices, standard CI/CD compilation pipelines, container orchestration, and multi-threaded background workers that require a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM balance without dedicated GPU or high-throughput local disk demands.
description: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-16xCPU-64GB is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by 16 shared AMD EPYC 7542 vCPUs at 2.0 GHz and 64.0 GB of system memory. It provides a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB RAM per core on the x86_64 architecture under KVM virtualization. The instance includes no bundled local storage and zero GPUs, requiring remote storage volumes for persistent data. Multi-core compute performance sits in the middle tiers, evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 15,148.0 and a PassMark CPU rating of 25,240.42. However, uncached write memory bandwidth and single-core stress-ng benchmarks register in lower performance bands, along with limited throughput for larger language model generation. This server is best suited for multi-threaded container workloads, CI/CD compilation, and horizontally scaled general application services.
